[39m   [38;2;181;189;217mIt began one winter when she barked into an empty quarry and heard her own voice return, softer and stranger, as though a second fox lived inside the stone. Delighted, she tried [39m      [38;2;145;152;161m┃
[39m   [38;2;181;189;217magain. The echo answered a little differently each time, and Marrow decided that no sound should ever vanish if she could help it.[39m                                                      [38;2;145;152;161m┃
[39m                                                                                                                                                                                           [38;2;145;152;161m┃
[39m   [38;2;181;189;217mShe kept her echoes in odd places. The hollow oak held the laughter of a passing owl. A cracked boot near the stream kept the whisper of rain. Under a flat rock, she stored the rumble[39m [38;2;145;152;161m┃
[39m   [38;2;181;189;217mof a distant train. Whenever she felt lonely, she visited her collection and listened.[39m                                                                                                  [38;2;145;152;161m┃
[39m                                                                                                                                                                                           [38;2;145;152;161m┃
[39m   [38;2;181;189;217mThe other animals thought her foolish. "You can't eat a sound," said the badger.[39m                                                                                                        [38;2;145;152;161m┃
[39m                                                                                                                                                                                           [38;2;145;152;161m┃
[39m   [38;2;181;189;217m"No," Marrow agreed, "but I can remember it."[39m                                                                                                                                           [38;2;145;152;161m┃
[39m                                                                                                                                                                                           [38;2;145;152;161m┃
[39m   [38;2;181;189;217mThen came the winter of the long silence. Snow buried the wood so deeply that the birds fell quiet and the stream froze mute. The animals grew restless and afraid, for without [39m        [38;2;240;246;252m┃
[39m   [38;2;181;189;217mfamiliar noise, the world felt as if it had stopped breathing.[39m                                                                                                                          [38;2;240;246;252m┃
[39m                                                                                                                                                                                           [38;2;240;246;252m┃
[39m   [38;2;181;189;217mMarrow trotted out into the white hush and began to visit her hiding places. At the oak, she barked once, and the owl's laughter rolled out through the trees. At the boot, rain [39m       [38;2;240;246;252m┃
[39m   [38;2;181;189;217mwhispered across the snow. Under the rock, the far-off train rumbled like a promise that somewhere, things still moved.[39m                                                                 [38;2;240;246;252m┃
[39m                                                                                                                                                                                           [38;2;240;246;252m┃
[39m   [38;2;181;189;217mOne by one, the animals crept from their burrows. The badger stood with his mouth open. A young hare began to cry, then to smile. They listened all night, wrapped in the borrowed [39m     [38;2;240;246;252m┃
[39m   [38;2;181;189;217msounds of warmer days, and nobody felt alone.[39m                                                                                                                                           [38;2;240;246;252m┃
[39m                                                                                                                                                                                           [38;2;240;246;252m┃
[39m   [38;2;181;189;217mWhen spring finally cracked the ice, the stream sang for itself again, and the birds returned with their noisy arguments. But on the first warm morning, the badger appeared at [39m        [38;2;240;246;252m┃
[39m   [38;2;181;189;217mMarrow's den carrying an acorn cap full of honey.[39m                                                                                                                                       [38;2;240;246;252m┃
[39m                                                                                                                                                                                           [38;2;240;246;252m┃
[39m   [38;2;181;189;217m"Teach me to keep one," he said, a little shyly.[39m                                                                                                                                        [38;2;240;246;252m┃
[39m                                                                                                                                                                                           [38;2;240;246;252m┃
[39m   [38;2;181;189;217mMarrow grinned, her tail sweeping the dust. Together they climbed toward the quarry, listening for a sound worth saving.[39m                                                                [38;2;240;246;252m┃
